sources.title: Plan Municipal de Desarrollo 2022–2025
sources.supports: Nazas at the Durango–Coahuila boundary, generally dry local course with exceptional flows toward Mayrán, upstream impoundment and irrigation diversion.
sources.limits: Municipal-scale prose does not establish every bend, terminal extension, canal identity, contemporary flow event or natural mouth position.

correspondence.finding: The northern end follows the Forquilha II–Várzea do Boi–Tauá corridor, rather than the western Trici branch. The plan's infrastructure map carries Jaguaribe labels along this corridor, while its reservoir table explicitly calls the watercourse at Forquilha II and Várzea do Boi Carrapateiras. This supports representative-system identity with a retained upper-feeder distinction, not an assertion that the selected endpoint is the river's exact natural source.

South of Tauá the line follows the Arneiroz II setting, bends southeast toward Saboeiro, then continues east through the Jucás/Cariús and Iguatu settings into Orós and its eastward outlet. The readable infrastructure sheet and the older basin figure show this distinctive succession. The modeled line through reservoir water is not assigned a separate natural-channel name.

From the corridor east of Orós, the selected course turns north past the Salgado approach and Jaguaribe town, makes its westward middle bend, and then turns northeast through the Castanhão setting toward Jaguaribara. The Médio Jaguaribe sheet shows that continuous Jaguaribe corridor and separately draws the eastern Figueiredo drainage and western Riacho do Sangue approach. Those tributaries are not transferred to the selected line as aliases.

Below Castanhão the route continues northeast through the São João do Jaguaribe setting into the Limoeiro do Norte area. The downstream piece then follows the lower valley toward Jaguaruana, turns north by Itaiçaba and Aracati, and reaches the Fortim estuarine setting. The Médio sheet and Baixo Figure 3 join these successive reaches; the Baixo text independently identifies Jaguaribe as the main river from Peixe Gordo to its mouth.

The Baixo source separately identifies Palhano as a left-bank tributary and describes branching/meandering channels near the mouth. Its generalized map supports the lower-system correspondence but does not establish a distinct local name for each modeled channel, a current coastline intersection or a surveyed final mouth vertex.

correspondence: The actual cached route was inspected in full, including the western starting leg, southern loop, northeastward upper section, southward return to the second fragment, broad eastward middle loop and long northeastward lower course. All three selected fragments are modeled mainstem fragments.

The supporting 2017 technical report describes an official basin and subbasin framework prepared through the Honduran water-resources authority and its project partners. It explains that catchment names and boundaries classify drainage areas; that text alone is not evidence that every modeled channel in an area shares its basin name.

No readable original map was inspected before acquisitions stopped. Consequently no full source-object correspondence, individual feeder name, reservoir passage, precise name transition or coastal outlet identity is asserted.

correspondence.object_scope: The complete single cached mainstem fragment was inspected, from the long eastern northward leg through the alternating westward bends, including the northern high-latitude bend and the final western approach. There are no additional tributary fragments in this selected group.
correspondence.displayed_length_limit: Retained model display length, not independently established natural-river length.
correspondence.full_path_finding: The eastern leg and the long middle sequence lie in the mapped Inland Ice, southeast and south of Washington Land. The western approach runs toward the broad ice-margin sector mapped as Humboldt Gletscher beside Kane Basin. The source graticule, ice shading, margin shape and land/coast configuration were inspected for this actual line; a bounding box or prior Greenland finding was not substituted for it.
correspondence.map_interpretation: The sheet distinguishes the blue surface contours, dashed ice-thickness isopachs and grey sub-ice bedrock contours. They describe ice and terrain, not named river courses.
correspondence.name_limit: Neither the geological map nor the glaciology explanation identifies the whole model line as one named surface river, one subglacial river or a uniformly named glacier. Proximity to the printed Humboldt Gletscher label cannot convert that glacier name into a river identity. The exact terminal natural feature and present-day flow remain unassigned.
correspondence.historical_scope: Historical 1995 cartography and 2009 explanation supply feature-class context. No current ice-front location, contemporary discharge or hydrological connection is asserted.
correspondence.conclusion: Readable regional coverage is sufficient for the completed scope hold; retain null names and no automatic application. Positive natural-river identity evidence would be required before any later name assignment.

correspondence.finding: The long northward mountain leg west of Durango continues through the Santiago Papasquiaro setting. INEGI Map 11 depicts this corridor as Santiago, distinct from Río Chico to the southeast and the west-draining San Gregorio/Piaxtla systems. Map 10 supplies the corresponding narrow upper drainage setting. The selected southern tip is retained as an upper feeder extent, without asserting its exact local hydronym or the natural source of the named Santiago.

North of Santiago Papasquiaro, the selected route turns northeast in the mapped Ramos corridor after the separate Tepehuanes approach. It reaches the Lázaro Cárdenas reservoir setting from the southwest. The map shows Sextín arriving separately from the northwest. CONANP identifies the Ramos–Sextín confluence at the Lázaro Cárdenas/El Palmito setting as the beginning of Nazas. A modeled line through that impounded junction is not uniformly Santiago, Ramos or an independently named reservoir channel.

correspondence.scope: Middle Nazas and Francisco Zarco passage
correspondence.finding: The selected line leaves the Lázaro Cárdenas setting southeastward, makes its broad southern turn and then runs east toward Francisco Zarco. Its sequence of bends and the mapped San Juan junction context agree with INEGI's Nazas corridor. The subsequent northward turn and approach to Lerdo correspond to the river below Francisco Zarco. CONANP independently places Nazas in Cañón de Fernández and distinguishes Francisco Zarco/Las Tórtolas from the upstream Lázaro Cárdenas reservoir. Exact reservoir-entry and name-transition vertices are not assigned.

correspondence.scope: Lower river and Mayrán terminal continuation
correspondence.finding: The selected lower course approaches the Lerdo–Gómez Palacio/Torreón setting and continues northeast and east toward San Pedro. INEGI's San Pedro hydrography map follows a separately labeled Nazas channel south of San Pedro through the San Miguel–San Nicolás setting, while distinguishing nearby irrigation canals. The modeled line continues farther east/northeast into the mapped Mayrán subbasin context than the named channel is depicted. The acquired sources do not establish that complete terminal extension as one named natural channel, a current wet river, or a surveyed salt-flat channel.

The Gómez Palacio municipal plan describes the local Nazas course as generally dry during the year, with exceptional flows toward Mayrán, and records upstream impoundment and irrigation diversion. That description explains why named river identity and present flow must be separated. The modeled continuation does not by itself prove continuous water, present-day connection across the terminal basin, or an exact historical shoreline.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
